chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from Ja'far ibn Nājīyah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about one who spent the nights of Mina in Mecca, and he said: 'Three from the livestock, he slaughters them.'

key_terms.الْغَنَمِ: Livestock (specifically sheep or goats in this context)
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: In Mecca (specifically referring to staying in the city rather than the camp of Mina)
key_terms.لَيَالِيَ مِنًى: Nights of Mina (the nights of 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.يَذْبَحُهُنَّ: He slaughters them (referring to the three animals)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for spending the nights of Mina in Mecca?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that a pilgrim who spends the nights of Mina in Mecca must offer three animals as expiation (kaffarah). This ruling highlights the importance of adhering to the prescribed rituals of Hajj, particularly the staying in Mina, and the consequences of deviating from them. The requirement of three animals underscores the significance of this ritual act in Shia jurisprudence.
